title.en: DNS: turning names into addresses

description.en: Understand how a name like www.google.com becomes an IP address, and why this “phone book” is split into layers and spread across many servers around the world.
description.zh: 弄懂 www.google.com 这样的名字怎样变成 IP 地址，以及为什么这本「电话簿」要分成层次、分散在全世界的很多服务器上。

name.en: The role of DNS: translating domain names into IP addresses (name resolution)
name.zh: DNS 的作用：把域名翻译成 IP 地址 (name resolution)

name.en: DNS's other services: host aliasing, mail server registry, load distribution
name.zh: DNS 的其他服务：别名、邮件服务器登记、负载分担 (host aliasing, mail server registry, load distribution)

name.en: The DNS namespace and how domain names are written
name.zh: DNS 名字空间与域名的写法 (DNS namespace and domain names)
资源记录 (resource records, RR) 与记录类型

name.en: Zones and zone name servers, and why not centralise
name.zh: 区与区名字服务器，为什么不集中 (zones, zone name servers, why not centralise)

name.en: The four kinds of name servers: root, TLD, authoritative, local
name.zh: 四类名字服务器：根、顶级域、权威、本地 (root, TLD, authoritative, local name servers)

name.en: The DNS name resolution process and caching
name.zh: DNS 解析过程与缓存 (DNS name resolution process and caching)
递归查询与迭代查询 (recursive vs iterative query)

name.en: Reading a dig answer for one DNS query
name.zh: 用 dig 看一次 DNS 查询的结果 (reading a dig answer)

description.en: Thinks DNS is one big table in a single server (or a group of servers); in fact it is a database distributed by layers across many servers around the world.
description.zh: 以为 DNS 是一台（或一组）总服务器里的一张大表；其实它是按层次分布在全世界很多服务器上的数据库。

description.en: Treats a zone and a domain as the same thing; a zone is a piece for administration, and can be smaller than a domain, because parts below it may have been delegated away.
description.zh: 把区 (zone) 和域 (domain) 当成一回事；区是管理上的一块，可以比域小，因为下面的部分可能已被委派出去。

description.en: Thinks the root server looks it all the way up for you; in fact it only gives referrals, and the local name server asks layer by layer.
description.zh: 以为根服务器会替你一路查到底；其实它只做转介，由本地名字服务器去一层层问。

description.en: Thinks the value of a CNAME is an IP address; in fact its value is another domain name, which must be resolved again to get the IP.
description.zh: 以为 CNAME 的值是 IP 地址；其实它的值是另一个域名，要再解析一次才得到 IP。

description.en: Thinks the larger number in an MX record has priority; in fact the smaller number has priority.
description.zh: 以为 MX 记录里数字大的优先；其实数字小的优先。

description.en: Thinks what is in a cache is always the latest; in fact, until the TTL expires, the cache does not know the authority has changed the record.
description.zh: 以为缓存里的永远是最新的；其实在 TTL 到期之前，缓存不会知道权威方已经改了记录。

description.en: Thinks there are only 13 root server machines in total; in fact there are 13 names, and behind each name are many machines.
description.zh: 以为根服务器一共只有 13 台机器；其实是 13 个名字，每个名字背后有很多台机器。

title.en: Take a guess first

prompt.en: You type www.google.com, and your computer must first turn this name into an IP address before it can send packets. Where do you think the table of all the world's “name → IP” pairs should be kept?
prompt.zh: 你输入 www.google.com，电脑得先把这个名字变成 IP 地址，才能把包发出去。全世界所有「名字 → IP」的对照表，你觉得应该放在哪里？

label.en: In one super server (or one machine room), and everyone asks it
label.zh: 放在一台超级服务器（或一个机房）里，所有人都去问它

feedback.en: It looks simplest. But everyone in the world would have to ask it first on every connection, and the traffic would be too much; and the moment it fails, the whole world can't get online.
feedback.zh: 看起来最简单。可是全世界每次上网都要先问它，流量扛不住；它一出故障，全世界就上不了网。

label.en: Every computer keeps its own complete copy of the table
label.zh: 每台电脑自己存一份完整的表

feedback.en: Names are added, removed and changed every day, and there is no way to update billions of devices at the same time.
feedback.zh: 名字天天有增、删、改，没法让几十亿台设备同时更新。

label.en: Spread over many servers, divided by the layers of the name, each in charge of a piece
label.zh: 分散在很多服务器上，按名字的层次分工，各管一块

feedback.en: Right, that is the design of DNS. Next we see how it divides the work, and why it divides it this way.
feedback.zh: 对，这就是 DNS 的设计。接下来看它怎样分工，以及为什么这样分。

label.en: In the routers, which translate names into IPs on the side
label.zh: 放在路由器里，路由器顺便把名字翻译成 IP

feedback.en: Routers forward packets by looking only at IP addresses; they don't understand application-layer names.
feedback.zh: 路由器只看 IP 地址来转发包，它不理解应用层的名字。

explain.en: Real DNS is the third option: the database is cut into many pieces, spread over many name servers, and the servers are arranged in layers, pointing the way one layer after another. Why it isn't kept on a single machine will be made clear point by point later.
explain.zh: 真实的 DNS 是第三种：数据库被切成很多块，分在很多名字服务器上，服务器之间按层次排列，一层层指路。为什么不放在一台机器里，后面会逐条讲清楚。

title.en: People remember names, routers recognise IPs
title.zh: 人记名字，路由器认 IP

text.en: Routers recognise only IP addresses, such as 121.7.106.83. They use addresses to address packets and choose routes, delivering them hop by hop (covered in Lesson 9). But you won't remember 121.7.106.83; what you remember is www.google.com.
text.zh: 路由器只认 IP 地址，比如 121.7.106.83。它用地址给包编址、选路，一跳一跳送过去（第 9 课讲过）。可你不会去记 121.7.106.83，你记的是 www.google.com。

text.en: So we need a phone book: give it a name, and it looks up the IP address. This phone book is DNS (Domain Name System).
text.zh: 那就需要一本电话簿：给一个名字，查出 IP 地址。这本电话簿就是 DNS (Domain Name System)。

text.en: Why not have everyone remember the IP directly, or write the IP into the web address? Because an IP is a location, while a name is an identity.
text.zh: 为什么不让大家直接记 IP，或者把 IP 写进网址里？因为 IP 是位置，名字才是身份。

items.en: **IPs change.** If a server moves to a different machine room or switches network provider, its IP changes; the name doesn't have to, as long as one line in the phone book is changed.
items.zh: **IP 会变。** 服务器搬了机房、换了网络服务商，IP 就变；名字不用变，只要电话簿里改一行。

items.en: **One name can map to many IPs.** Behind a big website there are many servers, each with an IP. The user only needs to remember one name.
items.zh: **一个名字可以对应多个 IP。** 大网站背后有很多台服务器，每台一个 IP。用户只需要记一个名字。

text.en: So DNS is an application-layer protocol: it maps human-readable domain names to the IP addresses that machines use. Other application-layer protocols such as HTTP, FTP and SMTP all ask it for help first.
text.zh: 所以 DNS 是一个应用层协议 (application-layer protocol)：把人读得懂的域名，映射成机器用的 IP 地址。HTTP、FTP、SMTP 这些别的应用层协议，都要先请它帮忙。

text.en: Note how it is implemented too: it is not a table on one machine, but a distributed database made up of many name servers arranged in a hierarchy. Why it is this way will come step by step later.
text.zh: 它的实现方式也要留意：不是一台机器里的一张表，而是一个分布式数据库 (distributed database)，由很多名字服务器 (name server) 按层次 (hierarchy) 组成。为什么要这样，后面会一步步讲到。

summary.zh: 超出课件：没有 DNS 之前

text.en: In the early days of ARPANET there weren't many hosts. All host names were kept in one file called HOSTS.TXT, maintained by one central party, and each machine downloaded it periodically. It worked well while machines were few; once there were many, the file couldn't be kept up to date, the download traffic was heavy, and duplicate names were hard to manage. In the early 1980s DNS replaced it.
text.zh: 早期的 ARPANET 主机不多。所有主机名放在一份叫 HOSTS.TXT 的文件里，由一个中心维护，各机器定期去下载。机器少的时候很好用；机器一多，文件更新不过来，下载的流量大，重名也难管。1980 年代初，DNS 取代了它。

text.en: Your computer still has a hosts file today, a relic of that era. The system usually checks it first before asking DNS.
text.zh: 你的电脑里至今还有一个 hosts 文件，就是那个年代留下的遗迹。系统一般会先查它，再去问 DNS。

title.en: One click, first ask DNS
title.zh: 一次点击，先问一句 DNS

text.en: You open www.unimelb.edu.au in your dorm. The browser has to send an HTTP request to that server, but all it has is the name. So before the first TCP packet goes out, there is a DNS query. This is called name resolution.
text.zh: 你在宿舍打开 www.unimelb.edu.au。浏览器要往这台服务器发 HTTP 请求，可它手里只有名字。所以在第一个 TCP 包发出去之前，先有一次 DNS 查询。这件事叫名字解析 (name resolution)。

alt.en: Five boxes connected in order: the browser takes the host name; the DNS client sends a query; the DNS server (marked with a question, which one); the reply contains the IP; the browser sets up a TCP connection to port 80 of that IP.
alt.zh: 五个方框依次相连：浏览器取出主机名；DNS 客户端发出查询；DNS 服务器（标着问号，是哪一台）；回复里是 IP；浏览器向该 IP 的 80 端口建立 TCP 连接。

caption.en: Name resolution comes before the TCP connection.
caption.zh: 名字解析在 TCP 连接之前。

text.en: A DNS client runs on the user's machine. The browser takes the host name from the web address and hands it over; the client sends out a query containing that host name; and finally it receives a reply containing the IP address. Only with the IP in hand does the browser start a TCP connection to port 80 of that IP (the handshake from the transport-layer lessons).
text.zh: 用户机器上跑着 DNS 客户端。浏览器从网址里取出主机名，交给它；它发出一个查询 (query)，里面是这个主机名；最终收到回复，里面是 IP 地址。拿到 IP，浏览器才向这个 IP 的 80 端口发起 TCP 连接（传输层那几课讲过的握手）。

text.en: One question to leave open: in step ③, which machine is the “DNS server”? If the phone book isn't on one machine, how does this machine know the answer? The second half of this lesson answers that. First we look at what else DNS can do, then at how names are arranged and records are stored.
text.zh: 留一个问题：第 ③ 步的「DNS 服务器」是哪一台？电话簿既然不在一台机器里，这台机器怎么知道答案？这一课的后半段就是回答它。先看 DNS 还能做什么，再看名字怎么排、记录怎么存。

title.en: Three other things DNS can do

text.en: Besides “name to IP”, DNS does three more things. Each of them corresponds to a kind of record in the database.
text.zh: 除了「名字变 IP」，DNS 还做三件事。每一件，在数据库里都对应一种记录。

text.en: Host aliasing
text.zh: 主机别名 (host aliasing)

text.en: A machine can have a real name that is hard to remember, and be given an easy-to-remember alias. The example in the slides: the canonical name is squizedge-cloud.cms.unimelb.edu.au, and the alias is www.unimelb.edu.au. You type the alias, DNS tells you the real name, and then gives the IP of the real name. The benefit: if the university changes its content platform one day, only the line the alias points to needs changing, and the name www.unimelb.edu.au stays the same. This uses the CNAME record.
text.zh: 一台机器可以有一个不好记的真名，再给它起好记的别名。课件里的例子：规范名 (canonical name) 是 squizedge-cloud.cms.unimelb.edu.au，别名是 www.unimelb.edu.au。你输入别名，DNS 告诉你真名，再给出真名的 IP。好处是：哪天学校换了内容平台，只改别名指向的那一行，www.unimelb.edu.au 这个名字不用变。用的是 CNAME 记录。

text.en: Mail server registry
text.zh: 邮件服务器登记 (mail server registry)

text.en: To send a letter to maria.read@unimelb.edu.au, the sender first has to find out: who is willing to receive mail for unimelb.edu.au? It takes the unimelb.edu.au after the @ and asks DNS, and gets one or several mail servers. This uses the MX record.
text.zh: 给 maria.read@unimelb.edu.au 发信，发送方要先找到：谁愿意收 unimelb.edu.au 的邮件？它取 @ 后面的 unimelb.edu.au 去问 DNS，得到一台或几台邮件服务器。用的是 MX 记录。

text.en: Load distribution and redundancy
text.zh: 负载分担与冗余 (load distribution and redundancy)

text.en: A big website has many servers, each with an IP. In DNS the same name can carry several A records. Each time the DNS server answers, it rotates the order of these addresses; the client generally takes the first one, so requests are spread across different servers. If one server is down, the client can still try the later addresses. When you read dig www.google.com later, you will see one name with 8 addresses.
text.zh: 大网站有很多台服务器，每台一个 IP。DNS 里同一个名字可以挂多条 A 记录。DNS 服务器每次回答时，轮换这些地址的顺序；客户端一般取第一个，请求就被摊到了不同的服务器上。某台宕机了，客户端还可以试后面的地址。后面读 dig www.google.com 时，你会看到一个名字有 8 个地址。

rows.en: The name is easy to remember and stable, and the real machine can be swapped
rows.zh: 名字好记又稳定，真正的机器可以换

rows.en: For one domain name, who receives its mail
rows.zh: 一个域名，谁来收它的邮件

rows.en: One name, with many servers behind it
rows.zh: 一个名字，背后多台服务器

rows.en: Several A records for the same name
rows.zh: 同一个名字的多条 A 记录

title.en: Which record to put

prompt.en: An online shop has only one name, www.shop.example, with 4 servers behind it. It wants visitors spread across the 4, and wants visitors to still get in when one of them is down. What is the most direct way to do this in DNS?
prompt.zh: 一家网店只有一个名字 www.shop.example，背后有 4 台服务器。它希望访客被分摊到 4 台上，而且其中一台宕机时，访客仍然能上。DNS 里最直接的做法是什么？

label.en: Put 4 A records on www.shop.example, one for each server
label.zh: 给 www.shop.example 放 4 条 A 记录，每台服务器一条

label.en: Put one MX record on www.shop.example
label.zh: 给 www.shop.example 放一条 MX 记录

feedback.en: MX only handles mail: it answers “who is willing to receive mail for this domain”, and has nothing to do with web access.
feedback.zh: MX 只管邮件：它回答「谁愿意收这个域的信」，和网页访问无关。

label.en: Put one CNAME on www.shop.example, pointing to one of the servers
label.zh: 给 www.shop.example 放一条 CNAME，指向其中一台服务器

feedback.en: A CNAME is an alias, and one alias points to only one canonical name, still the same machine, so it can't share the load. Also its value is a name, not an IP.
feedback.zh: CNAME 是别名，一个别名只指向一个规范名，还是同一台机器，分担不了负载。而且它的值是名字，不是 IP。

label.en: Write the 4 IPs into an NS record
label.zh: 把 4 个 IP 写进 NS 记录

feedback.en: The value of an NS record is the name of a name server, used to point the way. A web server's address goes in an A record.
feedback.zh: NS 记录的值是名字服务器的名字，用来指路。网页服务器的地址要放在 A 记录里。

explain.en: The same name can have several A records. DNS rotates the order of its answers, and the client generally uses the first, so requests are spread over different servers; if one is down, the client can switch to another address.
explain.zh: 同一个名字可以有多条 A 记录。DNS 轮换回答的顺序，客户端一般用第一个，请求就分到了不同的服务器；一台宕机，客户端还能改连另一个地址。

title.en: Names arranged as a tree

text.en: Names can't be a tangled mess. DNS arranges names into a tree, called the namespace. The root of the tree is at the top and has no name; below the root are the top-level domains (TLD).
text.zh: 名字不能是一团乱麻。DNS 把名字排成一棵树，叫名字空间 (namespace)。树根在最上面，没有名字；根的下面是顶级域 (top-level domain，TLD)。

alt.en: The DNS namespace tree: below the root are the generic top-level domains com, edu, org and the country top-level domains au, jp, uk and so on. Under edu is washington, below it cs and eng, and under cs is robot. Under au is edu, below it unimelb, and then www; the red line marks the path www.unimelb.edu.au.
alt.zh: DNS 名字空间的树：根下面是通用顶级域 com、edu、org 和国家顶级域 au、jp、uk 等。edu 下有 washington，其下有 cs 和 eng，cs 下有 robot。au 下有 edu，其下有 unimelb，再下是 www，红线标出 www.unimelb.edu.au 这条路径。

caption.en: Each box is a node in the tree, and a domain name is the path from a node up to the root.
caption.zh: 每个方框是树上的一个节点，域名就是从节点走到根的路径。

text.en: Top-level domains come in two kinds: generic domains, such as com, edu, gov, org, net; and country domains, such as au, jp, uk, nl. Below that, each organisation divides things up itself: under edu is washington, under washington is cs, under cs is robot.
text.zh: 顶级域分两类：通用域 (generic)，如 com、edu、gov、org、net；国家域 (country)，如 au、jp、uk、nl。再往下由各机构自己分：edu 下有 washington，washington 下有 cs，cs 下有 robot。

text.en: Read a domain name from right to left. www.unimelb.edu.au: start from the root, first to au (Australia), then edu (educational institutions), then unimelb, and finally the machine www. Each segment to the left narrows the scope by one level. In the figure there is another level edu under au, a second-level domain that the country domain divides for itself; Japan writes ac.jp and co.jp, and each country divides differently.
text.zh: 读一个域名，要从右往左。www.unimelb.edu.au：从根出发，先到 au（澳大利亚），再到 edu（教育机构），再到 unimelb，最后是机器 www。每往左一段，范围就缩小一层。图里 au 下面还有一层 edu，这是国家域自己分的二级域；日本的写法是 ac.jp、co.jp，各国分法不同。

text.en: Why layers? Because each organisation only needs to look after the names below itself. As long as names don't repeat under the same parent domain, there are no duplicates on the whole internet. Under washington.edu there is cs, and under vu.nl there is also a cs, without conflict: their full names are different.
text.zh: 为什么要分层？因为每个机构只需要管好自己下面的名字。名字只要在同一个父域下不重复，整个互联网就不会重名。washington.edu 下有 cs，vu.nl 下也有 cs，互不冲突：它们的完整名字不一样。

title.en: Rules for writing domain names

items.en: **Case-insensitive**: WWW.UniMelb.EDU.AU and www.unimelb.edu.au are the same name.
items.zh: **不分大小写**：WWW.UniMelb.EDU.AU 和 www.unimelb.edu.au 是同一个名字。

items.en: **Length limits**: each component is at most 63 characters, and the whole domain name at most 255 characters.
items.zh: **长度有上限**：每一段 (component) 最多 63 个字符，整条域名最多 255 个字符。

items.en: **Can be internationalised**: since 1999, domain names are no longer limited to English letters.
items.zh: **可以国际化**：从 1999 年起，域名不再限于英文字母。

text.en: There is also a pair of concepts: absolute and relative domain names.
text.zh: 还有一对概念：绝对域名和相对域名。

rows.en: The dot stands for the root. The name is counted from the root and pins down its exact position in the tree.
rows.zh: 这个点代表根。名字从根数起，指明它在树里的确切位置。

rows.en: Gives only part of the position, and can only be used in the context of some absolute domain name.
rows.zh: 只给出部分位置，只能放在某个绝对域名的上下文里用。

text.en: For example, on a machine in the domain cs.vu.nl., writing www means www.cs.vu.nl., and writing flits means flits.cs.vu.nl.. In the database on the next page, the first column is written with exactly this kind of relative name.
text.zh: 比如在 cs.vu.nl. 这个域里的机器上，写 www 就是 www.cs.vu.nl.，写 flits 就是 flits.cs.vu.nl.。下一页的数据库里，第一列写的正是这种相对名字。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: where 63 and 255 come from
summary.zh: 超出课件：63 和 255 从哪来

text.en: Inside a message, a domain name is stored segment by segment, and before each segment is 1 byte recording its length. The top two bits of that byte are used for something else, leaving 6 bits, so the maximum is 63. The whole domain name together with these length bytes is at most 255 bytes; written in ordinary text, the longest is about 253 characters. The exam follows the slides: 63 and 255.
text.zh: 域名在报文里是一段一段存的，每段前面有 1 个字节记录长度。这个字节的高两位另有用途，只剩 6 位，最大就是 63。整条域名连同这些长度字节，一共不超过 255 个字节；按平常的文字写法，最长约 253 个字符。考试按课件：63 和 255。

summary.en: Table of top-level domains (lots of detail, no need to memorise conceptually)
summary.zh: 顶级域表（细节多，概念上不必背）

text.en: The slides also list a table of top-level domains (in the history of the internet there have been more than two hundred and fifty). Conceptually you only need to remember: top-level domains are of two kinds, generic and country; some are restricted, available only to qualifying organisations, such as edu. Whether to memorise this table is as said in class.
text.zh: 课件还列了一张顶级域表（互联网历史上有两百五十多个顶级域）。概念上只需要记住：顶级域分通用域和国家域两类；有的受限，只给符合条件的机构用，比如 edu。要不要背这张表，以课上说的为准。

title.en: What the database stores is resource records
title.zh: 数据库里存的是资源记录

text.en: What a name server stores is called a resource record (RR). Each record is a five-tuple:
text.zh: 名字服务器里存的东西，叫资源记录 (resource record，RR)。每条记录是一个五元组：

rows.en: Which name this record is about
rows.zh: 这条记录说的是哪个名字

rows.en: For how many seconds at most this record may be cached
rows.zh: 这条记录最多可以被缓存多少秒

rows.en: IN means the internet; other classes are deprecated
rows.zh: IN 表示互联网，其他类别已弃用

rows.en: The content; its meaning changes with the type

text.en: TTL is time to live, in seconds. 86400 seconds = 24 × 60 × 60, exactly one day. It is what the authority says to caches: “You may trust this record for a day at most; after that, please come and ask me again.” For records that rarely change, the TTL can be long; for records that change often, the TTL must be short. Its use will show up when we get to caching.
text.zh: TTL 是 time to live，单位是秒。86400 秒 = 24 × 60 × 60，正好一天。它是权威方对缓存说的话：「这条记录你最多可以信一天，之后请重新来问我」。很少变的记录，TTL 可以长；常变的记录，TTL 要短。后面讲缓存时会看到它的用处。

text.en: Common types
text.zh: 常见的类型

rows.zh: 128 位整数（第 10 课的 IPv6）

rows.en: Canonical name: this name is an alias, and the real name is in the value
rows.zh: 规范名 (canonical name)：这个名字是别名，真名在值里

rows.en: Another domain name, not an IP
A priority, plus the domain name willing to receive mail; the smaller number has priority
rows.zh: 优先级，加上愿意收信的域名；数字小的优先

rows.en: The name of a name server for this domain
rows.zh: 这个域的名字服务器的名字

items.en: **PTR**: pointer. Looks up a name from an IP (reverse lookup), and the value is a domain name. It is not an “alias of an IP address”.
items.zh: **PTR**：指针。用 IP 反过来查名字（反向查询），值是一个域名。它不是「IP 地址的别名」。

items.en: **SPF**: a mail-sending policy written as text.
items.zh: **SPF**：用文字写下的邮件发送策略。

items.en: **SRV**: the host that provides a given service.
items.zh: **SRV**：提供某项服务的主机。

items.en: **TXT**: a piece of descriptive text.
items.zh: **TXT**：一段说明文字。

title.en: Reading a real zone database
title.zh: 读一份真实的区数据库

text.en: Below is a section of the cs.vu.nl database. Read it line by line, and you will meet all the types described so far.
text.zh: 下面是 cs.vu.nl 数据库里的一段。逐行读一遍，前面讲的类型就都见到了。

blocks.code:
; Authoritative data for cs.vu.nl
cs.vu.nl.     86400  IN  SOA    star boss (9527,7200,7200,241920,86400)
cs.vu.nl.     86400  IN  MX     1 zephyr
cs.vu.nl.     86400  IN  MX     2 top
cs.vu.nl.     86400  IN  NS     star

star          86400  IN  A      130.37.56.205
zephyr        86400  IN  A      130.37.20.10
top           86400  IN  A      130.37.20.11
www           86400  IN  CNAME  star.cs.vu.nl
ftp           86400  IN  CNAME  zephyr.cs.vu.nl

flits         86400  IN  A      130.37.16.112
flits         86400  IN  A      192.31.231.165
flits         86400  IN  MX     1 flits
flits         86400  IN  MX     2 zephyr
flits         86400  IN  MX     3 top

rowboat              IN  A      130.37.56.201
                     IN  MX     1 rowboat
                     IN  MX     2 zephyr

little-sister        IN  A      130.37.62.23

laserjet             IN  A      192.31.231.216

caption.en: Names in the first column such as star and www are relative names; add cs.vu.nl. to get the full name.
caption.zh: 第一列的 star、www 等是相对名字，补上 cs.vu.nl. 才是完整的名字。

items.en: **The first column holds relative names.** star means star.cs.vu.nl., because the whole database belongs to the zone cs.vu.nl.
items.zh: **第一列是相对名字。** star 就是 star.cs.vu.nl.，因为整份数据库属于 cs.vu.nl 这个区。

items.en: **The lines for cs.vu.nl. itself.** The NS says the zone's name server is star. The two MX lines say: mail sent to cs.vu.nl goes first to zephyr (priority 1), and if it is not available, to top (priority 2). The SOA holds the zone's parameters.
items.zh: **cs.vu.nl. 自己的几条。** NS 说这个区的名字服务器是 star。两条 MX 说：发给 cs.vu.nl 的信，先交给 zephyr（优先级 1），它不在，再交给 top（优先级 2）。SOA 是这个区的参数。

items.en: **star, zephyr and top each have an A record** giving their IPs.
items.zh: **star、zephyr、top 各有一条 A**，写着它们的 IP。

items.en: **www and ftp are CNAMEs.** www.cs.vu.nl is just an alias for star, and ftp is an alias for zephyr. If the website moves to another machine one day, only the www line needs to change.
items.zh: **www 和 ftp 是 CNAME。** www.cs.vu.nl 只是 star 的别名，ftp 是 zephyr 的别名。哪天网站搬到另一台机器，只要改 www 这一行。

items.en: **flits has two A records**: this machine has two addresses, connected to two networks. Its three MX lines: it receives mail itself first, if not, try zephyr, and if not, try top.
items.zh: **flits 有两条 A**：这台机器有两个地址，连着两个网络。它的三条 MX：先自己收，不行找 zephyr，再不行找 top。

items.en: **rowboat's MX**: it receives mail itself, otherwise hands it to zephyr. Here zephyr acts as a mail gateway.
items.zh: **rowboat 的 MX**：自己收，否则交给 zephyr。zephyr 在这里充当邮件网关。

items.en: The TTL is 86400 seconds throughout, one day. The lines after that don't write a TTL, so the default applies.
items.zh: TTL 都是 86400 秒，一天。后面几行没有写 TTL，按默认值。

title.en: The MX number is a priority

body.en: The smaller number has priority. 1 is tried before 2. The number is not a “count”, and it is not “bigger is better”.
body.zh: 数字小的优先。1 比 2 先试。数字不是「个数」，也不是「越大越好」。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: the string of numbers in the SOA
summary.zh: 超出课件：SOA 里那串数字

text.en: star is the primary name server of the zone, and boss is the administrator's mailbox (boss@cs.vu.nl). The five numbers in the brackets are, in order: the serial number (incremented each time the database changes, so replicas know a new version exists), the refresh interval, the retry interval, the expiry time, and the minimum TTL; apart from the serial number, the units are all seconds. The exam does not require reading it closely.
text.zh: star 是这个区的主名字服务器，boss 是管理员的邮箱（boss@cs.vu.nl）。括号里五个数依次是：序列号（每改一次数据库加一，让副本知道有新版本）、刷新间隔、重试间隔、过期时间、最小 TTL；除序列号外单位都是秒。考试不要求细读。

title.en: Who gets the mail first

prompt.en: In the cs.vu.nl database, rowboat has one A record (130.37.56.201) and two MX records: priority 1 points to rowboat, priority 2 points to zephyr. Someone sends mail to someone@rowboat.cs.vu.nl. To whom will the sender's mail program first try to deliver it?
prompt.zh: cs.vu.nl 的数据库里，rowboat 有一条 A 记录（130.37.56.201），和两条 MX 记录：优先级 1 指向 rowboat，优先级 2 指向 zephyr。有人给 someone@rowboat.cs.vu.nl 发邮件，发送方的邮件程序会先尝试把信交给谁？

label.en: First to rowboat; if it can't be reached, then to zephyr
label.zh: 先交给 rowboat；它连不上，再交给 zephyr

label.en: First to zephyr, because 2 is bigger than 1 and bigger has priority
label.zh: 先交给 zephyr，因为 2 比 1 大，大的优先

feedback.en: The direction is reversed. The number before the MX is a priority, and the smaller number is tried first.
feedback.zh: 方向反了。MX 前面的数字是优先级，数字越小越先试。

label.en: To both at once, whichever receives it first gets it
label.zh: 同时交给两台，谁先收到算谁的

feedback.en: The mail program tries them in priority order; once one is willing to accept it, it won't hand it to another.
feedback.zh: 邮件程序按优先级依次试，一台肯收，就不会再给另一台。

label.en: It doesn't look up MX, and uses 130.37.56.201 from the A record directly
label.zh: 不查 MX，直接用 A 记录里的 130.37.56.201

feedback.en: What mail needs to find is “who is willing to receive mail for this name”, and that is the job of the MX record. Here the top-priority MX happens to be rowboat itself, but this step can't be skipped: the machine that receives the mail can differ from the one the name belongs to, for example handing it to the mail gateway zephyr.
feedback.zh: 发邮件要找的是「谁愿意收这个名字的信」，那是 MX 记录的事。这里最优先的 MX 碰巧是 rowboat 自己，但这一步不能省：收信的机器可以和名字不是同一台，比如交给邮件网关 zephyr。

explain.en: The mail program first looks up the MX records of the recipient's domain name and tries them in order of number from small to large: priority 1 is rowboat itself, and if that fails, it then tries priority 2, zephyr.
explain.zh: 邮件程序先查收信人域名的 MX 记录，按数字从小到大依次尝试：优先级 1 是 rowboat 自己，不通再试优先级 2 的 zephyr。

title.en: A zone and a domain are not the same thing

text.en: The namespace is a tree, and of course it is not run by a single person. DNS cuts the tree into non-overlapping pieces, each called a zone. Each zone has one or more name servers, the hosts that store this zone's database, and they are authoritative for the zone: for names in this zone, their answers are the final source.
text.zh: 名字空间是一棵树，管理它的人当然不是一个。DNS 把树切成互不重叠的块，每块叫一个区 (zone)。每个区有一个或多个名字服务器，它们是存放这个区数据库的主机，对这个区是权威的 (authoritative)：关于这个区的名字，以它们的回答为最终来源。

alt.en: A subtree going down from edu: under edu is washington, under washington are cs and eng, and under cs is robot. Colours show the zones: edu is a zone by itself; washington and eng belong to the washington.edu zone; cs and robot belong to another zone, and the line from washington to cs is marked as delegation.
alt.zh: 一棵从 edu 往下的子树：edu 下是 washington，washington 下有 cs 和 eng，cs 下是 robot。颜色表示分区：edu 自己一个区；washington 和 eng 属于 washington.edu 区；cs 和 robot 属于另一个区，在 washington 到 cs 的连线上标着委派。

caption.en: The pink dashed box holds one zone, containing only cs and robot.
caption.zh: 粉色虚线框里是一个区，只含 cs 和 robot。

text.en: Look at the pink zone in the figure: it contains only cs and robot. How was it carved out? The administrator of washington.edu handed the names below cs to the computer science department to manage itself; this is called delegation. After delegation, the servers of washington.edu no longer store the data below cs, and only note “go and ask the servers over at cs”.
text.zh: 看图里的粉色区：它只含 cs 和 robot。它是怎么被切出来的？washington.edu 的管理员把 cs 以下的名字交给计算机系自己管，这叫委派 (delegation)。委派之后，washington.edu 的服务器就不再保存 cs 以下的数据，只记着「去问 cs 那边的服务器」。

text.en: So: a **domain** is a subtree of the tree; the domain washington.edu includes all the names under it, with cs, eng and robot all inside. A **zone** is a piece for administration: the zone washington.edu contains only washington and eng, because everything below cs has been delegated away. A zone can be smaller than a domain.
text.zh: 所以：**域**是树上的一棵子树，washington.edu 这个域包括它下面所有的名字，cs、eng、robot 都在内。**区**是管理上的一块：washington.edu 这个区只含 washington 和 eng，因为 cs 以下已经委派出去了。区可以比域小。

text.en: Why does a zone often have several name servers? If one fails, the others can still answer.
text.zh: 一个区为什么常有好几台名字服务器？一台出了故障，别的还能回答。

title.en: What “authoritative” means

body.en: The slides write “always correct”. A more accurate meaning: it is the final source of this zone's data, and replicas and caches elsewhere defer to it.
body.zh: 课件写「始终正确」。更准确的意思是：它是这个区数据的最终来源，别处的副本和缓存都以它为准。

title.en: Who answers authoritatively

prompt.en: The administrator of washington.edu has delegated the names below cs.washington.edu to name servers run by the computer science department itself. Now we want the A record of robot.cs.washington.edu. Who can give the authoritative answer?
prompt.zh: washington.edu 的管理员把 cs.washington.edu 以下的名字，委派给计算机系自己运营的名字服务器。现在要查 robot.cs.washington.edu 的 A 记录，谁能给出权威的回答？

label.en: The name servers of the washington.edu zone
label.zh: washington.edu 区的名字服务器

feedback.en: Everything below cs has been delegated away, so the servers of washington.edu no longer store that data; at most they will tell you “go and ask over at cs”.
feedback.zh: cs 以下已经委派出去，washington.edu 的服务器不再保存这部分数据，它最多告诉你「去问 cs 那边」。

label.en: The name servers of the cs.washington.edu zone
label.zh: cs.washington.edu 区的名字服务器

label.en: The root name servers
label.zh: 根名字服务器

feedback.en: The root knows only the name servers of each top-level domain; it does not store records for specific machines such as robot.
feedback.zh: 根只知道各顶级域的名字服务器，它不保存 robot 这种具体机器的记录。

label.en: The university's local name server
label.zh: 学校的本地名字服务器

feedback.en: A local server has at most a cache. A cache is a copy given by someone else, not authoritative data.
feedback.zh: 本地服务器最多有缓存。缓存是别人给的副本，不是权威数据。

explain.en: After delegation, the data of the zone cs.washington.edu is stored by the computer science department's own servers, and they are the authority for these names. The servers above only give referrals, and caches are only copies.
explain.zh: 委派之后，cs.washington.edu 这个区的数据由计算机系自己的服务器保存，它们是这部分名字的权威。上面的服务器只负责转介，缓存只是副本。

title.en: Why not centralise

text.en: Back to the question at the start. What if the whole phone book were kept on one machine? The slides list four problems, which together add up to poor scalability (does not scale well). For each one, the hierarchy has a corresponding answer.
text.zh: 回到开头那道题。如果把整本电话簿放在一台机器里，会怎样？课件列了四个问题，合起来就是扩展性差 (does not scale well)。每一个，层次结构都有对应的办法。

head.zh: DNS 的层次结构怎样解决

rows.en: Everyone in the world asks it first on every connection, and one machine can't cope
rows.zh: 全世界每次上网都先问一遍，一台机器扛不住

rows.en: Queries are spread over the servers of each zone; the local name server's cache then blocks most repeated questions
rows.zh: 查询分散到各个区的服务器；本地名字服务器的缓存再挡掉大部分重复的问题
单点故障 (single point of failure)

rows.en: If this one breaks, the whole world can't get online
rows.zh: 这一台坏了，全世界都上不了网

rows.en: Each zone has several servers, and the root has many replicas; if one place fails, the others are still there
rows.zh: 每个区有多台服务器，根也有很多副本；一处出事，别处还在
数据库离用户太远 (distant database)

rows.en: If it were on the other side of the Earth, every query would pay a very long round trip
rows.zh: 若放在地球另一边，每次查询都要付一个很长的往返

rows.en: The local name server is in your university or network provider, and a cache hit hardly has to leave the building
rows.zh: 本地名字服务器就在你的学校或网络服务商里，命中缓存几乎不用出门

rows.en: Even changing one name means going to the same centre
rows.zh: 改一个名字都要找同一个中心

rows.en: Delegation: each organisation manages its own zone, and changing its own records doesn't need begging anyone
rows.zh: 委派：每个机构管自己的区，改自己的记录不用求别人

text.en: In a sentence: the hierarchy cuts both “looking up” and “changing” into small pieces, each handled nearby. This is also why DNS can bear today's scale.
text.zh: 一句话：分层让「查」和「改」都被切成小块，各自就近处理。这也是为什么 DNS 能扛住今天的规模。

title.en: Four kinds of name servers

text.en: There are three kinds of servers in the hierarchy, plus one that sits outside the hierarchy but that you deal with every day.
text.zh: 层次结构里有三类服务器，外加一类在层次之外、却天天打交道的。

head.en: What it is in charge of

rows.en: The starting point of resolution; know the name servers of every top-level domain
rows.zh: 解析的起点，知道每个顶级域的名字服务器

rows.en: A referral to a top-level domain server: its name (NS record), plus its IP (glue record)
rows.zh: 转介 (referral) 到顶级域服务器：它的名字（NS 记录），加上它的 IP（glue 记录）

rows.en: com, org, net, edu and so on, and all country top-level domains such as uk, fr, au, jp
rows.zh: com、org、net、edu 等，以及 uk、fr、au、jp 等所有国家顶级域

rows.en: A referral to the authoritative servers of the zones below
rows.zh: 转介到它下面各个区的权威服务器

rows.en: An organisation's own DNS servers, which store and serve the authoritative records in its zone
rows.zh: 机构自己的 DNS 服务器，存放并提供自己区里的权威记录

rows.en: The answer itself; or a further referral to a zone below
rows.zh: 答案本身；或者再转介到更下面的区

rows.en: Not strictly part of the hierarchy. Each network provider, company or university usually has a default name server
rows.zh: 不严格属于层次。每个网络服务商、公司、学校通常有一个默认的名字服务器

rows.en: Answers directly if it has a cache; otherwise acts as a proxy and asks the upper layers for you
rows.zh: 有缓存就直接回；没有就当代理，替你向上层问

text.en: A referral means: “I don't know the answer, but go and ask it.” The root server won't tell you the IP of robot.cs.washington.edu. It will only say: edu is looked after by a.edu-servers.net, go and ask it, and here is its IP as well.
text.zh: 转介的意思是：「我不知道答案，但你去问它。」根服务器不会告诉你 robot.cs.washington.edu 的 IP。它只会说：edu 归 a.edu-servers.net 管，你去问它，它的 IP 也一起给你。

text.en: That “here is its IP as well” is the glue record. Why is it needed? Suppose the name server of example.com is called ns1.example.com. To send it a query, you must first know its IP; but to find out the IP of ns1.example.com you must ask the name server of example.com, which is itself. That is a dead loop. So when the level above gives the referral, it conveniently attaches this server's IP, breaking the loop.
text.zh: 那个「它的 IP 也一起给你」就是 glue 记录。为什么需要它？假设 example.com 的名字服务器叫 ns1.example.com。要给它发查询，得先知道它的 IP；可要知道 ns1.example.com 的 IP，又得去问 example.com 的名字服务器，也就是它自己。这是个死循环。所以上一级在转介时，顺手把这台服务器的 IP 一起附上，打破循环。

summary.zh: 超出课件：「13 个根服务器」

text.en: The slides say there are 13 root name servers worldwide, which is a simplified statement. More exactly, there are 13 names (a.root-servers.net through m.root-servers.net), and behind each name are many machines spread around the world. The same IP address is announced from many places at once, and your query is sent to the nearest one.
text.zh: 课件说全球有 13 个根名字服务器，这是简化的说法。准确地说，是 13 个名字（a.root-servers.net 到 m.root-servers.net），每个名字背后有很多台机器，分布在世界各地。同一个 IP 地址在多个地方同时发布，你的查询会被送到离你最近的一台。

text.en: Why 13? A common explanation: in early DNS a UDP message was at most 512 bytes, which was just enough to hold the names and addresses of 13 servers.
text.zh: 为什么是 13 个？常见的解释是：早期 DNS 的 UDP 报文最长 512 字节，刚好装得下 13 个服务器的名字和地址。

title.en: Following one query all the way

text.en: Now put the pieces together. The example in the slides: the machine filts.cs.vu.nl wants the IP of robot.cs.washington.edu. It doesn't go to the root itself, but first goes to its local name server (cs.vu.nl).
text.zh: 现在把前面的东西合起来。课件里的例子：filts.cs.vu.nl 这台机器要查 robot.cs.washington.edu 的 IP。它自己不去问根，而是先找本地名字服务器（cs.vu.nl）。

The initiator queries the local name server; the local server asks the root server, the edu server, the UW server and the UWCS server in turn; the first three each reply with a referral (NS for edu plus glue, NS for washington.edu, NS for cs.washington.edu), and the last answers with the A record for robot.cs.washington.edu; the local server returns the answer containing the IP to the initiator, and the initiator then connects directly to the target host.
alt.zh: 一次 DNS 解析的时序图，共 11 步。发起方向本地名字服务器查询；本地服务器依次问根服务器、edu 服务器、UW 服务器、UWCS 服务器，前三个各回一个转介（edu 的 NS 加 glue、washington.edu 的 NS、cs.washington.edu 的 NS），最后一个回答 robot.cs.washington.edu 的 A 记录；本地服务器把含 IP 的答案回给发起方，发起方再直接连接目标主机。

caption.en: Dark arrows are queries, blue arrows are answers. The slides' original figure has a typo in the target name (aashington), corrected here.
caption.zh: 深色箭头是查询，蓝色箭头是回答。课件原图里目标名字有一处笔误（aashington），这里已改正。

text.en: Notice what comes back at each step, more specific each time:
text.zh: 注意每一步回来的东西，一步比一步具体：

rows.en: Referral: the NS record for edu (a.edu-servers.net), plus its IP (glue)
rows.zh: 转介：edu 的 NS 记录（a.edu-servers.net），加上它的 IP（glue）

rows.en: Referral: the name server of washington.edu
rows.zh: 转介：washington.edu 的名字服务器

rows.en: Referral: the name server of cs.washington.edu
rows.zh: 转介：cs.washington.edu 的名字服务器

rows.en: Answer: the A record of robot.cs.washington.edu
rows.zh: 答案：robot.cs.washington.edu 的 A 记录

text.en: Only the last step is the answer; the first three are all “go and ask it”. As the local name server asks its way down, it caches every mapping it learns. In step 10 it hands the A record containing the IP to the initiator; in step 11 the initiator takes the IP and connects to the target host.
text.zh: 只有最后一步是答案，前面三步都是「去问它」。本地名字服务器一路问下来，学到的映射都会缓存 (cache)。第 10 步，它把含 IP 的 A 记录交给发起方；第 11 步，发起方拿着 IP 去连接目标主机。

title.en: How long the cache keeps things, and how queries travel
title.zh: 缓存存多久，查询怎么传

text.en: Every record the local name server learns, it caches: not only the final answer, but also the NS for edu and the NS for washington.edu picked up along the way. When the next person asks the same name, it answers directly. Asking for another .edu name, it can also skip the root and go straight to the edu servers. So in the real world, the root servers are rarely asked.
text.zh: 本地名字服务器每学到一条记录，就缓存起来：不只是最后的答案，路上拿到的 edu 的 NS、washington.edu 的 NS 也存着。下一个人来问同一个名字，直接回答。问另一个 .edu 的名字，也可以跳过根，直接去问 edu 的服务器。所以真实世界里，根服务器很少被问到。

text.en: How long does the cache keep a record? It is decided by the record's own TTL. The TTL of each cached record counts down second by second, and at 0 it is thrown away, to be asked again next time.
text.zh: 缓存存多久？由记录自己的 TTL 决定。缓存里每条记录的 TTL 一秒一秒倒数，到 0 就丢掉，下次再去问。

text.en: This is a trade-off:
text.zh: 这是个权衡：

items.en: **Long TTL**: more cache hits, faster queries, less work for the authoritative servers; but when an administrator changes a record, it takes a long time before the whole world sees it.
items.zh: **TTL 长**：缓存命中多，查询快，权威服务器也省力；但管理员改了记录，要过很久全世界才看得到。

items.en: **Short TTL**: changes take effect quickly; but caches can't hold on to anything, so there are more queries.
items.zh: **TTL 短**：改动很快生效；但缓存留不住，查询多。

text.en: So an administrator who is about to change a website's IP often lowers the TTL beforehand.
text.zh: 所以准备给网站换 IP 的管理员，常常会提前把 TTL 调小。

text.en: How does the query itself travel? DNS usually runs on UDP port 53. One question and one answer, with a very small message; setting up a TCP connection for it first would cost 1 extra RTT for the handshake alone, which isn't worth it (the trade-off in Lesson 12, “UDP and TCP”). UDP doesn't care about loss, so a lost query is resent by the DNS client itself.
text.zh: 查询本身怎么传？DNS 通常跑在 UDP 的 53 端口上。一问一答，报文很小，若为它先建一条 TCP 连接，光握手就要多花 1 个 RTT，不划算（第 12 课「UDP 与 TCP」里的那个取舍）。UDP 不管丢包，所以丢了的查询，由 DNS 客户端自己重发。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: when the answer is too big
summary.zh: 超出课件：回答太大的时候

text.en: Traditionally, a DNS answer over UDP is at most 512 bytes. When it doesn't fit, the server puts a “truncated” flag in the answer, and the client asks again over TCP. The later EDNS extension can relax this limit, and in the dig output you will see a line udp: 4096.
text.zh: 传统上，UDP 的 DNS 回答最多 512 字节。放不下时，服务器在回答里带上「已截断」的标志，客户端改用 TCP 再问一遍。后来的 EDNS 扩展可以放宽这个上限，你在 dig 的输出里会看到一行 udp: 4096。

text.en: In addition, browsers and operating systems have a small cache of their own, which is checked before asking the local name server.
text.zh: 另外，浏览器和操作系统自己也有一份小缓存，在问本地名字服务器之前先查。

title.en: The stale answer in the cache

prompt.en: A website's A record has a TTL of 300 seconds. The university's local name server cached it at second 0. At second 100, the website's administrator changed this name to point to a new IP. At second 130, a student looks up this name. What will the local server reply?
prompt.zh: 某个网站的 A 记录，TTL 是 300 秒。学校的本地名字服务器在第 0 秒缓存了它。第 100 秒，网站管理员把这个名字改指向了新 IP。第 130 秒，有同学来查这个名字。本地服务器会回什么？

label.en: The new IP: the cache automatically syncs with the authoritative server
label.zh: 新 IP：缓存会自动和权威服务器同步

feedback.en: A cache does not sync on its own. Until the TTL expires, it doesn't know at all that the authority has changed.
feedback.zh: 缓存不会主动同步。在 TTL 到期之前，它根本不知道权威方改了。

label.en: The old IP: the record is still within its TTL, so it answers from the cache
label.zh: 旧 IP：记录还在 TTL 有效期内，直接用缓存回答

label.en: It first asks the authoritative server to confirm, then answers
label.zh: 先去问权威服务器确认，再回答

feedback.en: That would be the same as having no cache. The whole point of a cache is not having to ask again within the TTL.
feedback.zh: 那就等于没有缓存了。缓存的意义，正是在 TTL 内不用再问。

label.en: It can't answer, because the record has been changed
label.zh: 无法回答，因为记录已经被改了

feedback.en: The local server doesn't know the record was changed; the cache in its hands is still valid, so it can answer, only the answer is out of date.
feedback.zh: 本地服务器并不知道记录被改了，它手里的缓存仍然有效，所以能回答，只是答案已经过时。

explain.en: This is the price of the TTL: before it expires, a cache may give an out-of-date answer. Only at second 300, when the cache entry expires, will the local server ask again and get the new IP. That is why an administrator who wants to change an IP often lowers the TTL beforehand.
explain.zh: 这是 TTL 的代价：在到期之前，缓存可能给出过时的答案。要等到第 300 秒缓存失效，本地服务器才会重新去问，拿到新 IP。所以要换 IP 的管理员，常常提前调小 TTL。

title.en: Recursive and iterative: who runs errands for whom
title.zh: 递归与迭代：谁替谁跑腿

text.en: Look again at those 11 steps: they hide two different ways of asking.
text.zh: 再看刚才那 11 步，里面藏着两种不同的问法。

items.en: **Recursive query**: the server that is asked gets the mapping for the client, rather than giving only part of the answer. “Please look it up all the way for me and tell me when you have it.”
items.zh: **递归查询** (recursive query)：被问的服务器替客户端把映射查到手，而不是只给部分答案。「请你替我查到底，查到了再告诉我。」

items.en: **Iterative query**: the server that is asked only replies “I don't know this name, but go and ask this server”, giving the next server to ask.
items.zh: **迭代查询** (iterative query)：被问的服务器只回答「我不知道这个名字，但你去问这个服务器」，给出下一个要问的服务器。

alt.zh: 发起方通过蓝色箭头向本地服务器发出递归查询并最终得到答案；本地服务器通过红色双向箭头依次向根、edu、UW、UWCS 四个服务器发出迭代查询，前三个回转介，最后一个回答案。

caption.en: The same 11-step process, split into two blocks by the way of asking.
caption.zh: 同一个 11 步过程，按问法分成两块。

text.en: Matching them up: initiator to local server is recursive: it sends once, and waits for the final answer. The local server asking upward to the root, edu, UW and UWCS is iterative: each stop replies with only a referral, and the local server takes the referral itself and asks the next stop.
text.zh: 对应起来：发起方到本地服务器，是递归：它只发一次，等着拿最终答案。本地服务器往上问根、edu、UW、UWCS，是迭代：每一站只回一句转介，本地服务器自己拿着转介，去问下一站。

text.en: Why do upper-layer servers like the root generally do only iterative? Think about it: local servers all over the world come to ask the root. If the root had to chase every query all the way to the end for each of them, it would have to hold a huge number of unfinished queries at the same time, and would soon collapse. Iterative lets the root reply with just a referral, fast and cheap. The legwork is left to each network's own local server, and those also carry caches, so the more they are used, the more they save.
text.zh: 为什么根这样的上层服务器，一般只做迭代？想想看：全世界的本地服务器都来问根。如果根要替每一个查询一路追到底，它得同时挂着海量没做完的查询，很快撑不住。迭代让根只回一句转介，又快又省。跑腿的活，交给每个网络自己的本地服务器，它们还带着缓存，用得越多越省。

title.en: Which query is used by whom on whom

prompt.en: In the 11-step resolution above, which statement is correct?
prompt.zh: 在上面 11 步的解析里，下面哪个说法对？

label.en: The initiator's query to the local name server is recursive; the local name server's queries to the root, edu, UW and UWCS are iterative
label.zh: 发起方对本地名字服务器是递归查询；本地名字服务器对根、edu、UW、UWCS 是迭代查询

label.en: It is recursive throughout: the root server looks it up for the local server all the way to the authoritative server
label.zh: 全程都是递归：根服务器替本地服务器一路查到权威服务器

feedback.en: The root won't chase it all the way for you; it only replies with a referral. If the whole world's queries were chased to the end by the root, it couldn't cope.
feedback.zh: 根不会替你一路追到底，它只回一句转介。要是全世界的查询都让根追到底，它撑不住。

label.en: It is iterative throughout, including from the initiator to the local server
label.zh: 全程都是迭代，包括发起方到本地服务器

feedback.en: The initiator sends one query and waits for the final answer, and all the referrals in between are handled by the local server. That is exactly recursive: the party asked looks it up all the way for you.
feedback.zh: 发起方只发一次查询，就等着拿最终答案，中间的转介全由本地服务器处理。这正是递归：被问的一方替你查到底。

label.en: The local server is recursive toward the root and iterative toward the initiator
label.zh: 本地服务器对根是递归，对发起方是迭代

feedback.en: Exactly the opposite. For the initiator it looks the answer up all the way (recursive); for servers like the root, it can only get a referral and then go ask the next stop itself (iterative).
feedback.zh: 正好反了。对发起方，它替人查到底（递归）；对根等服务器，它只能拿到转介，再自己去问下一站（迭代）。

explain.en: Look at this point to see who runs errands for whom: does the server that is asked get the answer itself and then reply (recursive), or does it only point the way and let the other party go and ask again (iterative). Initiator to local server is the former, and local server to the servers in the hierarchy is the latter.
explain.zh: 谁替谁跑腿看这一点：被问的服务器是自己把答案查到手再回（递归），还是只指路让对方自己再去问（迭代）。发起方 → 本地服务器是前者，本地服务器 → 层次里的各服务器是后者。

title.en: Reading one dig: what a real answer looks like
title.zh: 读一次 dig：真实的回答长什么样

text.en: dig is a command-line tool that prints DNS's answer as it is. Below is the output of dig www.google.com; read it section by section against what we have covered.
text.zh: dig 是个命令行工具，能把 DNS 的回答原样打印出来。下面是 dig www.google.com 的输出，一段一段对着前面讲的东西读。

caption.zh: 课件里的 dig 输出，略去了开头两行。

rows.en: Query type QUERY, status NOERROR (success); flags qr (this is an answer), rd (the client asked for recursion), ra (the server supports recursion); then the record counts of each section
rows.zh: 查询类型 QUERY，状态 NOERROR（成功）；标志 qr（这是一条回答）、rd（客户端要求递归）、ra（服务器支持递归）；后面是各段的记录数

rows.en: 8 records, all with TTL 283 seconds, the IPs are a group 142.251.15x.119
Who the authoritative name servers of this domain are
rows.zh: 这个域的权威名字服务器是谁

rows.en: 4 NS records: ns1 to ns4.google.com, TTL 91419 seconds
rows.zh: 4 条 NS：ns1 到 ns4.google.com，TTL 91419 秒

rows.en: Useful information attached on the side
The A and AAAA records of these 4 servers, saving you from looking them up
rows.zh: 这 4 台服务器的 A 和 AAAA 记录，省得你再去查

text.en: A few places worth stopping to think about:
text.zh: 几个值得停下来想的地方：

items.en: **One name, 8 addresses.** This is the load distribution mentioned earlier: the same www.google.com has a group of servers behind it.
items.zh: **一个名字，8 个地址。** 这就是前面说的负载分担：同一个 www.google.com，背后有一组服务器。

items.en: **The additional section is a relative of glue.** The authority section gives only names like ns1.google.com, and the additional section brings their IPs along, so you don't need another round of asking.
items.zh: **附加段就是 glue 的亲戚。** 权威段只给了 ns1.google.com 这样的名字，附加段把它们的 IP 一起带来，免得你再问一轮。

items.en: **Why is the answer's TTL 283 while the NS's TTL is 91419?** Two reasons. One is that the records' original TTLs differ: a website's address may change often because of scheduling, so its TTL is short; name servers almost never change, so the TTL can be very long (91419 seconds is about 25 hours). The other is that when you query through a local server, dig shows how many seconds this record has left in the cache, and the number may differ each time you query.
items.zh: **为什么答案的 TTL 是 283，而 NS 的 TTL 是 91419？** 两个原因。一是记录本来的 TTL 就不同：网站的地址可能因为调度常常变，TTL 短；名字服务器几乎不变，TTL 可以很长（91419 秒约 25 小时）。二是通过本地服务器查时，dig 显示的是这条记录在缓存里还剩多少秒，每次查到的数字都可能不同。

summary.en: Beyond the slides: small details in the header
summary.zh: 超出课件：头部里的小细节

text.en: On an error, status becomes another value, for example NXDOMAIN means this name does not exist. ADDITIONAL: 9 is 1 more than the 8 records listed below it; the extra one is the OPT pseudo-record, which is the EDNS extension itself.
text.zh: 出错时，status 会变成别的值，比如 NXDOMAIN 表示这个名字不存在。ADDITIONAL: 9 比下面列出的 8 条多 1，多出来的是 OPT 伪记录，也就是 EDNS 扩展本身。

title.en: If all DNS servers crash at once
title.zh: 如果所有 DNS 服务器同时崩溃

prompt.en: Suppose all the DNS servers in the world crash at the same moment, and all caches are lost too. What effect does this have on your use of the internet? What can still be done and what cannot? Say why.
prompt.zh: 假设全世界所有 DNS 服务器在同一时刻崩溃，缓存也全部失效。这对你上网有什么影响？哪些事还能做，哪些不能？说说为什么。

key_points.en: Names can no longer be translated into IP addresses (name resolution fails)
key_points.zh: 名字无法再翻译成 IP 地址（名字解析失效）

key_points.en: If you already know the IP address, accessing by IP directly still works, because IP routing and TCP themselves are not broken
key_points.zh: 如果已经知道 IP 地址，直接用 IP 访问仍然可以，因为 IP 路由和 TCP 本身没有坏

key_points.en: Most people can't remember servers' IPs, so getting online by name hardly works, and the internet is effectively close to paralysed
key_points.zh: 绝大多数人记不住服务器的 IP，所以靠名字上网几乎行不通，上网实际上近乎瘫痪

key_points.en: Services that depend on names (such as finding a mail server through an MX record) are also affected
key_points.zh: 依赖名字的服务（如按 MX 记录找邮件服务器）也会受影响

model_answer.en: After DNS crashes, domain names can no longer be translated into IP addresses. The network itself is not broken: IP routing and TCP connections still work, so if you know a server's IP, typing the IP straight into the browser still gets you there. But most people can't remember those IPs and normally get online by name, so in practice the internet is almost unusable. Services such as mail, which rely on names (MX records) to find servers, would fail along with it.
model_answer.zh: DNS 崩溃之后，域名就不能再翻译成 IP 地址了。网络本身没有坏：IP 路由、TCP 连接都还能用，所以如果你知道服务器的 IP，直接在浏览器里输入 IP 仍然能访问。可是绝大多数人记不住那些 IP，平时都靠名字上网，所以实际上几乎没法用互联网。邮件之类要靠名字（MX 记录）找服务器的服务，也会跟着失效。

explain.en: DNS is only responsible for translating names into IPs; it does not carry data. When it breaks, the road is still there, but you don't know the house number of the destination. Those who know the house number (the IP) can still go, but almost nobody can memorise them, so the impact is enormous.
explain.zh: DNS 只负责把名字翻译成 IP，它不负责传数据。它坏了，路还在，只是你不知道目的地的门牌号。知道门牌号（IP）的还能去，但几乎没人能背得下来，所以影响极大。

title.en: Back to that click in the dorm

text.en: Walk through this lesson along that click on www.unimelb.edu.au:
text.zh: 把这一课沿着 www.unimelb.edu.au 那次点击走一遍：

items.en: The browser takes the host name from the web address and hands it to the DNS client.
items.zh: 浏览器从网址里取出主机名，交给 DNS 客户端。

items.en: The DNS client sends a **recursive query** to the university's **local name server**, over UDP port 53.
items.zh: DNS 客户端向学校的**本地名字服务器**发一个**递归查询**，走 UDP 的 53 端口。

items.en: The local server checks its **cache**. If it isn't there, it asks upward **iteratively**: the root refers to the au servers, and referrals follow down the tree until the **authoritative server** of unimelb.edu.au. (How many levels of delegation there are below au depends on the real configuration.)
items.zh: 本地服务器查**缓存**。没有，就**迭代**着往上问：根转介到 au 的服务器，往下依次转介，直到 unimelb.edu.au 的**权威服务器**。（au 往下具体有几层委派，以真实的配置为准。）

items.en: The authoritative server answers. In the slides' example www.unimelb.edu.au is an alias, so it first gives the canonical name, then the A record for it.
items.zh: 权威服务器回答。课件的例子里 www.unimelb.edu.au 是个别名，先给出规范名，再给出它的 A 记录。

items.en: The local server stores the record in its cache, for as long as the **TTL** decides, and returns the IP to the browser.
items.zh: 本地服务器把记录存进缓存，存多久由 **TTL** 决定，再把 IP 交回浏览器。

items.en: With the IP in hand, the browser starts a TCP connection to its port 80.
items.zh: 浏览器拿着 IP，向它的 80 端口发起 TCP 连接。

rows.en: Translates human-readable names into the IPs machines use; a database distributed by layers
rows.zh: 把人读的名字翻译成机器用的 IP，是按层次分布的数据库

rows.en: Aliases, mail server registry, load distribution
rows.zh: 别名、邮件服务器登记、负载分担

rows.en: A tree, read from right to left; split into generic and country domains
rows.zh: 一棵树，从右往左读；分通用域和国家域

rows.en: A five-tuple: name, TTL, class, type, value
rows.zh: 五元组：名字、TTL、类别、类型、值

rows.en: A zone is a piece for administration; delegation hands a subtree to someone else to manage
rows.zh: 区是管理上的一块，委派把子树交给别人管

rows.en: Root, top-level domain and authoritative servers only refer or answer; the local server runs errands for you and caches
rows.zh: 根、顶级域、权威只负责转介或回答；本地服务器替你跑腿并缓存

rows.en: The client is recursive toward the local server; the local server is iterative going upward
rows.zh: 客户端对本地服务器递归；本地服务器往上迭代

text.en: Only after getting the IP can the browser start the TCP connection and begin requesting the page. The next lesson, “The Web and HTTP”, takes it from there: how many round trips a page needs.
text.zh: 拿到 IP 之后，浏览器才能发起 TCP 连接，开始请求页面。下一课「万维网与 HTTP」接着往下走：一个页面要多少个往返。
